subject: Linear combination of coefficients of one model as covariate for other models

messages.author: adc8ca6cfb4e05df
messages.subject: Linear combination of coefficients of one model as covariate for other models
parts:
Dear all, 

I'm finding a way, perhaps similar to this approach in the FAQ, to do the as the title.

More specifically, let say we have

y1 = time + X, time = {1, 2, 3, 4}
 
I'd like the second likelihood of the form

y2 =  (time_3 - time_2) + X

y2 does not exist in any other times than the time_3

Does that make sense and is there a way to code this for a two likelihood model?

Thanks,
Kinh

It's not an offset but a covariate, to estimate a coefficient of the change in y1 on y2. Time is a fixed effect in the above illustration, but in real data I would use random walk or AR alike, 

I attempt to simulate as a simplified version as

g = 4 # number of time points, can be ~20 in real data
N = 4000 # total sample size, can be 500K
n = N/4 # sample size per period
t = rep(1:g, each = n) # real data will be random walk/AR...
Y1 = 1 + 1.1 * t + rnorm(N) # outcome 1
Y2 = 0.5 + 2.0 * (Y1[t==3] - Y1[t==2]) + rnorm(n) # outcome 2

Then arrange the data as
